title: Isaiah Chapter 66 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 66 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 66 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 66.

questions.question: In Isaiah 66, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool
He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man
A voice of noise from the city
Before she travailed, she brought forth
questions.correctAnswer: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:1 states, 'The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool' first in the chapter.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 66:1, what does the LORD say the heaven is?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:1 says, 'The heaven is my throne.'

questions.question: Who will the LORD look to, according to Isaiah 66:2?
options: Him that is poor and of a contrite spirit
Those who build houses for Him
Those who bring lambs for sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Him that is poor and of a contrite spirit
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:2 states, 'but to this man will I look, even to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 66:3, what is the action compared to killing a man?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:3 states, 'He that killeth an ox is as if he slew a man.'

questions.question: What consequence does the LORD say He will bring upon those who did evil and did not answer His call in Isaiah 66:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:4 says, 'I also will choose their delusions, and will bring their fears upon them.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 66:5, who said, 'Let the LORD be glorified'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:5 states, 'Your brethren that hated you... said, Let the LORD be glorified.'

questions.question: What kind of voice is mentioned in Isaiah 66:6?
options: A voice of noise from the city
questions.correctAnswer: A voice of noise from the city
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:6 mentions 'A voice of noise from the city.'

questions.question: In Isaiah 66:7, what is said about the woman before she travailed?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:7 states, 'Before she travailed, she brought forth.'

questions.question: What question does Isaiah 66:8 ask about the earth?
options: Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day?
Shall the earth be destroyed by fire?
Shall the earth be covered with water?
Shall the earth be silent forever?
questions.correctAnswer: Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:8 asks, 'Shall the earth be made to bring forth in one day?'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 66:1, what question does the LORD ask regarding the house and place of rest?
options: Where is the house that ye build unto me?
Who shall build the house for me?
When will the house be finished?
Why build a house for me?
questions.correctAnswer: Where is the house that ye build unto me?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:1 asks, 'Where is the house that ye build unto me? and where is the place of my rest?'

questions.question: In Isaiah 66:3, what is burning incense compared to?
options: As if he blessed an idol
As if he made an offering to God
As if he built an altar
questions.correctAnswer: As if he blessed an idol
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:3 states, 'he that burneth incense, as if he blessed an idol.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 66:2, who made all things?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:2 says, 'For all those things hath mine hand made.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 66:5 says that the brethren who cast out the faithful will be ashamed.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:5 states, 'but he shall appear to your joy, and they shall be ashamed.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 66:7 describes a woman delivering a man child before she experienced pain.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:7 says, 'Before her pain came, she was delivered of a man child.'

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 66:4 says the LORD will bless those who chose evil before His eyes.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:4 states the LORD will bring delusions and fears upon those who did evil, not bless them.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 66 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 66 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the LORD say about bringing forth in Isaiah 66:9?
options: He will cause it to happen.
He will not bring to birth.
questions.correctAnswer: He will cause it to happen.
questions.explanation: This is correct because Isaiah 66:9 states that the LORD asks whether He will bring to the birth and not cause to bring forth, implying that He will indeed cause it to happen.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 66:10 promise will happen if someone loves Jerusalem?
options: They will rejoice for joy with her.
They will be comforted in her.
questions.correctAnswer: They will rejoice for joy with her.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:10 encourages those who love Jerusalem to rejoice for joy with her, indicating a promise of shared joy.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 66:11, what will the people be satisfied with?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:11 states that people will suck and be satisfied with the breasts of her consolations, indicating a source of comfort and nourishment.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 66:12, what will the LORD extend to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:12 states that the LORD will extend peace to her like a river, illustrating the abundance of peace He will provide.

questions.question: How does the LORD promise to comfort His people in Isaiah 66:13?
options: As a father comforts his children.
As one whom his mother comforteth.
As a friend comforts a friend.
As a king comforts his subjects.
questions.correctAnswer: As one whom his mother comforteth.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:13 states that the LORD will comfort His people as a mother comforts her children, showing a nurturing and tender care.

questions.question: What reaction is promised in Isaiah 66:14 when the people see the LORD's actions?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:14 promises that when the people see the LORD's actions, their hearts shall rejoice, indicating a deep sense of gladness.

questions.question: What will the LORD come with according to Isaiah 66:15?
options: Fire and chariots like a whirlwind.
questions.correctAnswer: Fire and chariots like a whirlwind.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:15 declares that the LORD will come with fire and chariots like a whirlwind, emphasizing His power and judgment.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 66:16, by what means will the LORD plead with all flesh?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:16 states that the LORD will plead with all flesh by fire and by His sword, indicating a call to accountability and judgment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 66:3 say about sacrifices?
options: They are pleasing to the LORD.
They are of no value if done hypocritically.
They must be done with joy.
questions.correctAnswer: They are of no value if done hypocritically.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:3 illustrates that sacrifices done in hypocrisy are as unworthy as the acts of idolatry, emphasizing the need for sincerity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 66:4 reveal about the LORD's response to those who do evil?
options: He will bring their fears upon them.
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring their fears upon them.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:4 states that the LORD will choose delusions for those who did evil, highlighting His response to their actions.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 66:5 say about those who tremble at the LORD's word?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:5 indicates that those who tremble at the LORD's word will experience joy when the LORD appears.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 66:7 indicate about Zion's birth?
options: She will bring forth before she travailed.
She will give birth to twins.
questions.correctAnswer: She will bring forth before she travailed.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:7 reveals that Zion brought forth before her pain came, indicating a miraculous delivery.

questions.question: Is it true that the earth can bring forth in one day according to Isaiah 66:8?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:8 poses the question of whether a nation can be born in one day, suggesting the possibility of miraculous events.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD will comfort His people in Jerusalem as a father comforts his children according to Isaiah 66:13?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:13 specifically states that the LORD will comfort His people as one whom his mother comforteth, not as a father.

questions.question: Is it false that the LORD will come with fire according to Isaiah 66:15?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:15 clearly states that the LORD will come with fire, indicating His power and judgment.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 66 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 66.

questions.question: What shall happen to those who sanctify and purify themselves while eating swine's flesh according to Isaiah 66:17?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Isaiah 66:17, where the LORD declares that those who engage in these practices shall be consumed together.

questions.question: What does the LORD know according to Isaiah 66:18?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:18 reveals that the LORD knows the works and thoughts of people, indicating His omniscience.

questions.question: To which nations will the sign be sent according to Isaiah 66:19?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:19 mentions that the sign will be sent to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud among other nations.

questions.question: What will the brethren be brought as according to Isaiah 66:20?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:20 describes the brethren being brought as an offering to the LORD from all nations.

questions.question: What will the new heavens and new earth signify according to Isaiah 66:22?
options: They shall remain before the LORD
They will be a place of judgment
questions.correctAnswer: They shall remain before the LORD
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:22 emphasizes that the new heavens and new earth which the LORD will make shall remain before Him.

questions.question: How often will all flesh come to worship according to Isaiah 66:23?
options: From one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another
questions.correctAnswer: From one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:23 states that all flesh shall come to worship before the LORD from one new moon to another and from one sabbath to another.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'sanctify' in Isaiah 66:17 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'sanctify' (קדש, qadash) means to set apart as holy, which aligns with the context of Isaiah 66:17.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Isaiah 66:24 when describing the fate of the transgressors?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:24 employs symbolism, as the carcases and unquenchable fire symbolize judgment and the consequences of transgression.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of God's judgment expressed in Isaiah 66:17?
questions.explanation: Revelation 20:10 speaks of judgment and eternal punishment, echoing the theme present in Isaiah 66:17.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the promise of worship from all nations as seen in Isaiah 66:23?
questions.explanation: Revelation 7:9 depicts a great multitude from every nation worshiping before God, fulfilling the promise in Isaiah 66:23.

questions.question: What comes before Isaiah 66:17 regarding God's judgment?
options: A description of the new heavens
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:16 speaks of the LORD rendering judgment, preceding the specific warning in Isaiah 66:17.

questions.question: What comes after Isaiah 66:23 regarding the fate of the transgressors?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:24 follows Isaiah 66:23, describing the fate of the transgressors in detail.

questions.question: The new heavens and new earth mentioned in Isaiah 66:22 symbolize what in biblical theology?
questions.explanation: The new heavens and new earth signify God's promise of restoration and renewal, fulfilling His covenant.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 66:19 mentions that the sign will be sent to nations that have seen the LORD's glory.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:19 states that the sign will be sent to nations that have not heard His fame or seen His glory.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 66:20 details how the children of Israel will bring offerings in a clean vessel.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:20 mentions that the children of Israel will bring offerings in a clean vessel into the house of the LORD.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 66 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 66 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 66:2 teach about God's response to human humility and repentance?
options: God looks favorably on the poor and contrite in spirit who tremble at His word
God only accepts sacrifices and burnt offerings as true worship
God ignores the humility of the poor and prefers the proud
God accepts human works regardless of the heart condition
questions.correctAnswer: God looks favorably on the poor and contrite in spirit who tremble at His word
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:2 states that God will look to the man who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and trembles at His word, emphasizing the doctrine that God values humility and repentance over external offerings.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 66:3 teach about the nature of false worship and its equivalence to sin?
options: Offering forbidden sacrifices is as sinful as murder and idolatry
All sacrifices are acceptable to God if offered sincerely
Incense and offerings are always pleasing to God
God disregards the manner of worship as long as the heart is sincere
questions.correctAnswer: Offering forbidden sacrifices is as sinful as murder and idolatry
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:3 equates improper sacrifices and offerings to serious sins like murder and idolatry, indicating that false worship is deeply offensive to God.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 66:22 teach about the permanence of God's new creation and the continuity of His people?
options: The new heavens and new earth will remain forever, and so will the seed and name of God's people
God's creation is temporary and will be replaced frequently
The continuity of God's people depends on their works alone
The new creation is symbolic and not literal in permanence
questions.correctAnswer: The new heavens and new earth will remain forever, and so will the seed and name of God's people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:22 teaches that just as the new heavens and new earth will endure before God, so will the descendants and name of His people, affirming eternal covenant promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 66:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:18 states that God knows the works and thoughts of all people, demonstrating His attribute of omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 66:15 particularly highlight?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:15 describes the Lord coming with fire and chariots like a whirlwind to render His anger with fury and flames of fire, emphasizing God's wrath against sin.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 66:7-8 connect to the broader biblical theme of sudden, miraculous salvation and nation formation?
options: It prefigures the sudden birth of the Messiah and the rapid growth of the church
It refers exclusively to natural childbirth in Israel's history
It denies the possibility of sudden national restoration
It relates only to agricultural metaphors without theological significance
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the sudden birth of the Messiah and the rapid growth of the church
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:7-8 speaks of Zion bringing forth children in one day, symbolizing the miraculous and sudden nature of God's redemptive work, often applied theologically to the Messiah's birth and the church's expansion.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical theme does Isaiah 66:20-21 anticipate regarding God's plan for the Gentiles?
options: The inclusion of Gentiles in worship and priesthood
The exclusion of Gentiles from God's covenant
The Gentiles remaining in perpetual exile
The destruction of all Gentile nations
questions.correctAnswer: The inclusion of Gentiles in worship and priesthood
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:20-21 foretells that the Lord will bring brethren from all nations as offerings to Jerusalem and take some to be priests and Levites, indicating Gentile inclusion in God's covenant community.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 66:23 and Isaiah 66:24 teach about eschatological worship and judgment?
options: All flesh will worship regularly before God, and the wicked will face eternal judgment and abhorrence
Worship will cease in the new creation, and judgment will be temporary
Only Israel will worship God, and no eternal judgment exists
Eschatological worship is symbolic, and punishment is annihilation
questions.correctAnswer: All flesh will worship regularly before God, and the wicked will face eternal judgment and abhorrence
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:23-24 teach that from new moon to sabbath all flesh will worship the Lord, while those who transgress Him suffer eternal punishment, highlighting final judgment and universal worship.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 66:4 and Isaiah 66:17 teach about human rejection of God and divine judgment?
options: Those who reject God's call and engage in abominations will be consumed by His judgment
God will overlook idolatry if people sincerely repent afterward
False worship has no consequences in God's plan
Divine judgment is delayed indefinitely for the unrepentant
questions.correctAnswer: Those who reject God's call and engage in abominations will be consumed by His judgment
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:4 warns of God choosing their delusions and fears because they ignored Him, and 66:17 declares that those who sanctify themselves with abominations will be consumed, showing the certainty of judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 66:10 and Isaiah 66:13 teach about God's comfort and restoration of His people?
options: God comforts His people like a mother and calls them to rejoice in Jerusalem's restoration
God's comfort is limited to individual spiritual experience without communal restoration
Restoration will bring sorrow, not joy, according to these verses
Comfort and joy are unrelated to God's promises in these verses
questions.correctAnswer: God comforts His people like a mother and calls them to rejoice in Jerusalem's restoration
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:10 invites rejoicing with Jerusalem, and 66:13 compares God's comfort to a mother's comfort, teaching a doctrine of joyful restoration and divine consolation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Isaiah 66:7-9 teaches an impossible natural birth and nation formation. What does this passage actually teach?
options: God sovereignly brings about sudden and miraculous national restoration
It describes a purely natural childbirth with no divine intervention
It predicts that Zion will fail to bring forth her children
It denies God's role in the birth or restoration of a nation
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly brings about sudden and miraculous national restoration
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:7-9 rhetorically asks who has heard of such a thing, then affirms God's power to cause Zion to bring forth her children suddenly, teaching God's sovereign and miraculous intervention.

questions.question: What doctrine does Isaiah 66:6 teach about God's justice towards His enemies?
options: God will render recompense to His enemies decisively
God ignores the actions of His enemies
God will forgive all enemies unconditionally
questions.correctAnswer: God will render recompense to His enemies decisively
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:6 describes a voice from the Lord rendering recompense to His enemies, teaching the doctrine of God's righteous and decisive justice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Isaiah 66:9 demonstrate in God's promise to cause Zion to bring forth?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:9 affirms that God will not cause to bring forth and then shut the womb, demonstrating His sovereign control over life and national destiny.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Isaiah 66:19-20 make regarding the mission to the nations?
options: God sends survivors to proclaim His glory to distant nations, anticipating the missionary movement
God limits His glory to Israel alone
The nations are condemned without hope of hearing God's fame
Missionary outreach is not part of God's plan in this passage
questions.correctAnswer: God sends survivors to proclaim His glory to distant nations, anticipating the missionary movement
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:19-20 states God will send those who escape to distant nations to declare His glory, prefiguring the global mission to the Gentiles.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Isaiah 66:14 and Isaiah 66:16 teach about divine blessing and judgment?
options: God's hand is known in blessing His servants and executing judgment on His enemies
God's blessing and judgment are arbitrary and unrelated
God's judgment is merciful and lenient toward enemies
questions.correctAnswer: God's hand is known in blessing His servants and executing judgment on His enemies
questions.explanation: Isaiah 66:14 speaks of rejoicing and flourishing of God's servants, while 66:16 depicts judgment by fire and sword upon enemies, showing both blessing and judgment from God.
